chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Basir, from Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said:

Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not leave for people any proof against their souls except through the manifestation of the Imam. And the manifestation of the Imam is that He informs them of their names and their characteristics, and informs them that they are the allies of Allah, and that Allah has made obedience to them obligatory. And whoever does not know them dies on the day of his death as one ignorant, and whoever does not obey them dies on the day of his death as a disbeliever, and whoever does not show allegiance to them dies on the day of his death as one who turns back (from faith)."

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءُ اللَّهِ: Allies of God / Friends of God

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Imam as the 'Proof' of Allah in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this foundational doctrine of *al-Imamah* as a prerequisite for valid faith, emphasizing that the Imam serves as the necessary intermediary for divine guidance. This narration underscores the Shia view that recognition (*ma'rifah*) of the Imam's specific attributes and authority is not merely ceremonial but constitutive of one's spiritual state, where neglect leads to distinct categories of disbelief (*kufr*) or apostasy (*riddah*).
